_meta.description: Idempotently configure ONE existing GitHub personal-account budget on github.com/settings/billing/budgets: set 'Stop usage when budget limit is reached' and 'Receive budget threshold alerts' on or off. Hard-gates the budget's product, account, exact amount and GitHub's offered alert thresholds BEFORE touching anything. Never changes the amount or scope, never creates or deletes budgets. Probes current state, skips toggles already in the desired state, saves per toggle, and verifies from a fresh reload.
_meta.verifiedScope: Idempotent path (desired == live, no branch runs) and dry mismatch routing (apply_mode=_dry) were run live on eldrgeek's Actions budget, relay build 0.1.528. The LIVE toggle+save branches (stop_to_*, alerts_to_*) have NOT been exercised live, because the budget was already configured and flipping it off to test was not authorized. Treat the first real apply as a verification run.
_meta.author: Yeshie (Claude Opus 5, CCc) for Mike Wolf, 2026-09-13
_meta.riskNote: Changes billing configuration. The guard is the pre-change gate set (budget_id + product + account + exact amount + thresholds), not an 'assert false' first step. Note: 'assert' is not implemented in the compiled runtime (returns status 'unsupported', which does not stop a chain), so the README's assert-false guard pattern is a no-op.

auth.note: Chrome profile that owns the relay must be signed in as {{account}}. If GitHub asks for sudo mode, 2FA or a passkey, the post-save url gate times out and the run stops. A human completes that step.

params.base_url: https://github.com (also makes run-async's tab picker choose a github.com tab)
params.budget_id: UUID of the budget. From the edit URL (/settings/billing/budgets/<id>/edit) or the row menu's data-testid='delete-budget-<id>'.
params.product: Scope label shown on the edit form, e.g. 'Actions'. Hard gate.
params.account: GitHub login that owns the budget. Hard gate.
params.amount: Expected budget amount exactly as the input holds it, e.g. '20'. Hard gate. The recipe never types into this field.
params.thresholds: Alert thresholds. GitHub fixes these at 75/90/100% for personal budgets and offers ONE checkbox, so this is asserted as the form text '75%, 90%, and 100%', not configured.
params.alerts: 'on' or 'off' (the single 'Receive budget threshold alerts' checkbox)
params.apply_mode: '' for a live run, '_dry' to route mismatches to read-only branches and not fail the final check

anomalies: MISLEADING TEST ID: data-testid='alert-checkbox' is the STOP USAGE box (label[for] = 'Stop usage when budget limit is reached'). The alerts box has no test ID. Both have name='alert-checkbox'. Verified by reading label[for=<id>] on two separate page loads, 2026-09-13.
aria-checked on these checkboxes does not track :checked (present but not 'true' while checked). Use :checked only.

wait_for with a state/stateGraph never matches in this runtime (PRE_MATCH_WAIT_FOR is called with stateGraph=null and PRE_ASSESS_STATE is not in scope in the MAIN world, so it throws and is retried to timeout). All state checks here use assess_state; all hard gates are plain selector waits.
Branch steps cannot nest (onMismatch is handled in the outer chain loop only), so each toggle branch does its own save + reload.
No recipient field exists on the personal-account budget form. Alerts go to the account's billing email; the form cannot show or change recipients.

Budget rows on the list page carry no product-specific attributes, and the runtime has no safe text-row selector (find_row clicks the matched row), so the budget is addressed by budget_id and the product is asserted on the edit form.
_meta.verificationByConsequence: Re-read after a fresh navigate: the list row shows 'Stop usage Yes/No' and '$<amount> budget'; the edit form's :checked states match. A green toast is not proof.

chain._: PHASE 1 - Land on exactly one budget and prove it is the right one before touching anything

chain.note: HARD GATE: edit form rendered. A login, sudo or 2FA page fails here and the chain stops.
HARD GATE: exact amount. React keeps the value attribute in sync, so '20' cannot match '200'.
HARD GATE: GitHub still offers exactly these thresholds.
HARD GATE: stop-usage label present (see anomalies: it belongs to data-testid='alert-checkbox').
chain.text: Stop usage when budget limit is reached

chain._: PHASE 2 - Probe and fix each toggle only if it differs (this is what makes the recipe idempotent)

chain.note: Matched = already in desired state = no branch, no click.

chain.note: The real proof. Mismatch on a live run routes to a branch that throws.
Evidence: every budget row, including 'Stop usage Yes/No' and amount.
